answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity in cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Validating new nodes requires stake tied to consensus history, while redundant verification scales attacker costs superlinearly. If a malicious swarm blooms like wild yarrow across the network, automated slashing triggers exponential capital exhaustion. This traps attackers in an evaporating resource lagoon, unable to flood the vast economic ocean.
